And there's also an image on page 15 of the report where you can see the grave and the outlines of the robbing. That would be four pages ahead of this one. There you go; at the bottom there. There's also an image previous page where you can see the body location of the remaining bodies in the grave. In the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, we need this image for my next question. Would it be correct to say that the area that you have here contained the largest number of body, both the area marked Roman numeral I and number III, and was that an area that was included in the aerial images taken in September 1995? In other words, was this area already robbed at the time, or attacked.

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: This grave -- this is one grave. The images show the exact shape of this grave on the ground on both satellite images. So this -- everything that occurred here occurred in two moments, the initial interment or burial of the bodies, and the second time when some of the bodies were removed from the two areas that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question is: Is it a possible scenario that, in September, in the areas marked I and III in this sketch, bodies were buried? The bodies that you discovered in 2000 and dug out.

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: It is not a likely scenario. The grave is uniform on its borders. The bodies are co-mingled and show the same amount of decomposition. There is a continuation to this grave which shows that it is a single event that occurred. According to my estimates, the initial deposit between 19 -- between -- was it July 5th and July 27th of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What is the basis on which you are drawing this conclusion in terms of the timing of the burial, these specific bodies?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Well, these specific bodies are the bodies that are -- that make up the grave. The grave, the actual hole, is a hole that has continuation. It has uniformity. All of the body concentrations are at the same height. There are truncated bodies on the edges of the robbing areas in body concentration I, body concentration II, and body concentration III, which actually means that some probably large piece of equipment truncated those bodies while removing bodies that occupated those now empty areas. The depth of the grave is an average of 140. The bodies are -- they have no separate stratigraphy among them; in other words, they were deposited in a single event. So all those things lead me to believe that all of these bodies were put in there in a single event, and the bodies that are missing were taken out, like I said, probably in one event, but could be two, and that also created the body parts that were also found only around the areas where the robbing occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, did the investigators draw your attention at any point to the fact that this grave was located in the vicinity of the fiercest fighting in the summer of 1995 between the BH army column that was fighting its way through, on the one hand, and the Army of Republika Srpska, on the other?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I first -- did you pay attention at all whether the persons [indiscernible] were casualties from fighting or whether they were killed in another way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is an analysis that can be done. As a matter of fact, there is a way of doing it and that is by the analysis of trauma patterns and the location on the trauma. From my looking at these bodies, I can tell you that many of them had -- 89 of them had what appeared to be blindfolds around their heads, most of them directly around their eyes. We did not find weapons of fighting. The concentration of bullet cases that we found were only on one side. There didn't seem to be opposing concentration of bullet cases. There was nothing that I found that would lead me to believe that this was a result of -- of -- of a combat, and, again, to make that conclusion, you actually do have to go and look at the analysis of the bodies. You do expect to get only about two out of ten people suffering from fatal wounds in combat. This is published information. When you go over that amount of fatalities in a combat, it -- it's suggesting something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. -- But my question was mainly focussed on you did not make final determinations on whether they were war casualties -- I mean, war casualties -- I mean combat casualties or others but you have given us some observations which make you believe that it's unlikely that they were all - or most of them were - combat casualties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. I do not treat that in my report. However, I do have a point of view on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, the theory in this case is that the said bodies or part of the bodies were not the result of executions but, rather, that they were killed in action, not in this specific location but some 4 kilometres from this area in the forested region, and that the bodies have been collected during the hygiene and sanitation procedure, and then subsequently buried in this grave. My question is: From the point of view of your expertise and your knowledge that I asked you about at the beginning of my cross-examination, can one rule out this situation?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: This is a very complex question to answer only with archaeology. Once again, I must bring to your attention that to make that determination, which I don't make in this report because I don't have all the information but one must look at the analysis, the result of the analysis of the remains; one must look at the results of the identification process; one must look, again, at the analysis of the ballistics, and many other things that would help us to determine that specifically. However, from what I see here, the scenario in the grave and around the grave tells us that it doesn't coincide with that theory, mainly because of this large grouping of shell cases around one specific area of the body -- of the grave. However, if there is other evidence that suggests otherwise, it should be evaluated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Professor. Now I'd like to ask you this: Within the rules of your profession, is there any explanation why would anyone who is trying to conceal a crime would rob a grave in order to conceal the crime and leave so many bodies behind after having dug up the grave, opened it, and then put them back into the grave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object. This calls for speculation well beyond Mr. Peccerelli's area of expertise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, without having laid a foundation that part of the expertise of a witness is why someone would conceal or not conceal under certain circumstances, I think the question should not have been put to him. So if you want -- if you find it important enough, then you could consider to try to establish that. If not, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try, Your Honours. Could we again get P2552, page 4 in both English and B/C/S of the witness's report about Lazete 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will try to introduce you into this step by step. Did you deal with -- or did you estimate how many bodies were robbed from that grave? How many bodies were removed?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In Conclusion L, which I will read. It says: "The robbing excavation affected two areas, approximately 35 per cent of the entire grave. This suggests that if 127 bodies were recovered from approximately 65 per cent of the grave, and estimated total of 195 bodies were originally interred inside the grave. The approximate number of robbed bodies is 68."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this speculation about the number of bodies absent from the site while you are exhuming?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: This is a hypothesis for the search of the missing bodies from this grave from known secondary graves. The idea here was to establish a base-line so that we may look for those bodies using a mathematical equation to establish a probable missing number. And that's what it is, a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to acquaint yourself with the work of Professor Baraybar?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: If what you mean is have I read his reports, the answer is no. However, I did work under Jose Pablo Baraybar in 1997 and in 1998, both in Brcko and in some of the exhumation sites related to the Srebrenica case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, in the conclusion under item L, you make an estimate that the total number of bodies would be 195, if there had been no robbing of the grave.

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what L says.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Why am I asking? Could we please get P2088 on our screens. This is a report made by Professor Baraybar about Lazete 1, which we're now discussing and which you also worked on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please get page 8 in both B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor Baraybar says here that the preliminary results from the site of Lazete 1 are: "The calculation of the minimal number of individuals is 250." He testified here and explained the methodology used to arrive at this figure -- or, rather, number. I'm now asking you if your report preceded Professor Baraybar's in time. Was there a connection for the drawing of general conclusion? I mean, was there a connection between the two of you?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of when he presented his report, and we have never discussed this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me when I say that here, in this estimate, because both reports are based on estimates, there is a difference of over 25 percent of the number of bodies in Lazete 1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: The witness has already testified he's not familiar with this report, which includes the date, how it was done, methodology, what -- what Mr. Baraybar based the report on. Mr. Baraybar was here as a witness, available to talk about how he did that. And without further information put to this witness about those -- those factors, I don't see how he can make a judgement call about the differences in conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We were not yet, I think, at any question. There's a difference of over 25 percent. Okay. That was not yet a question, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Yes. Because the -- the -- the phrase that's being used in this report is this concept of a minimum number of individuals and that is not the same thing as what Mr. Peccerelli has been talking about in terms of bodies found, an estimation of bodies in the grave. They're slightly different and I'm sure he could go into it if asked. But it's comparing apples and oranges at this point to just show him one sentence about Lazete 1 without having any more information and ask him to make a -- I mean, we can all see these are different numbers and what the mathematical differentiation is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it seems that it -- we did not go any further than that yet. Whether the witness is able to give explanations, that is a different matter. But, Mr. Stojanovic, please keep mind that an analysis of all that, apart from saying one figure is 25 percent more than another figure, which doesn't tell us that much, that needs perhaps more thorough analysis. Proceed, as you deem fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I would like to consult my client for a brief moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While Mr. Stojanovic is consulting with Mr. Mladic, it would be helpful for the Prosecution to know whether the next witness, Mr. Rechner, will be required today. As the Chamber will recall, he was ill last week and he is not fully recovered and we would leave him at the hotel if he will not be called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we would not need him before tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I can continue, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, it is not our intention here to mix apples and oranges. My question was: Considering what you have just seen and the rule used to determine the minimum number of individuals in Lazete 1, can you, based on your expertise, tell us, whether you still stand by the estimate stated in your report; namely, that there were 195 bodies there in all?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Well, based on a the minimum number of individuals determined, obviously this is done with physical evidence. So my estimate obviously is under the number -- minimum number of individuals. However, I do have to say that - and this is to clarify - we label bodies and body parts. One of the body parts is also the loose bone bag and in the loose bone bag you have fragments of bodies, of fragments of bones which are later used to determine this minimum of individuals, so I would have to say that my estimate was low and that Mr. Jose Pablo Baraybar's estimates are based on the actual analysis of the remains. We were -- I was only there during the recovery and I had limited access to the information of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, perhaps I have not understood. Can you tell us if Professor Baraybar at any point had access to the report about the number of bodies that you found in Lazete 1? Or is his analysis based only on an analysis of a secondary site, or secondary sites, Hodzici 3 and 4?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first try to establish whether the witness has any knowledge about all this. And what you mean by bodies that you found in Lazete 1, is that the bodies that were exhumed and which were the basis for the extrapolation of the guess or the estimate of the others? Could you be precise? Do you have any knowledge about the basis, any detailed knowledge about the basis on a which Professor Baraybar based his numbers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have procedural knowledge, Your Honour, which every single body and body sheet, the bodies, the evidence, the rest of the evidence, and the body sheets were all loaded onto refrigerated containers, as well as other containers sent down to Visoko for the analysis which Mr. Jose Pablo Baraybar led. I expect that that's exactly what happened. If there are other secondary graves that derived from this one, that is exactly what would have happened as well. So he would have had information on all of these bodies to be able to make that determination without looking at my report, my report is limited in the overall picture of what happened because of these missing sections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand you well, in your view, Professor Baraybar would have had better information to come to more accurate numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's different information at different stages of the process. But to make a minimum number of individuals determination, then, yes, it is better information because he had the bodies in the morgue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, you mentioned that you found strips of cloth tied around the heads or -- of 89 individuals. Could you now take a look at a photograph from your report. I think it's P2552, and we need page 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the photograph we saw at the outset, Your Honours, when you started to -- or, rather, when the direct examination of the witness began. I would like the third photograph enlarged, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is one of the bodies or body parts you spoke about exhumed from Lazete 1. You told the Prosecutor that what we see is not a wire but a ribbon. Please tell us around which part of the body the ribbon is tied?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: This is a piece of cloth tied around the leg. I would have to look at the actual exhumation form to tell you which leg or if it's both. But it's -- it's the legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this piece of cloth or, rather, the body around which it is tied one of those 89 that you mentioned in your summary report about Lazete 1?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: I -- if -- if I may consult, I -- just from this image, this image is showing ligatures on other parts of the body differentiated from possible blindfolds. I don't know if this one had a possible blindfold on top of it. If it did, then, yes, it would be included; and, if no, it would not be included. May I look at the...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may look at your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the exhumation form, it only had a strip of material around the left leg. Then the right leg and going into the lower leg. So it's -- appears to be two pieces of material but one of them connects from the higher thigh to the knee area, as you can sort of make out in this image. So the answer is no, this one does not have a possible blindfold.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this one of the 89 bodies on which blindfolds were found as you stated in your report for Lazete 1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand your previous answer to be that this was because no blindfold was found that it's not among the 89 where you established that you found blindfolds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. This is not part of the 89.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic. And please try to focus your answers -- your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is a convenient time for a break. I can finish within ten minutes or even less. I have only two documents left to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest, since we started late, that is, we started a quarter to -- at 20 minutes to 1.00, that you use the last ten minutes of this one hour to complete your examination -- your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please get on our screens D339.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And while we wait for the document to appear, Professor, do you know that members of the BH army often wore ribbons round their heads or upper arms as a sign of -- as something to be recognised by?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: The first time I heard that was in my last testimony when Mr. Karadzic mentioned it. Prior to that, no, I had no knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us together take a look at a number of stills from this video-clip, which has already been used in this trial, and we can comment on them together.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you kindly open this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document is -- do we need a specific page or --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Here it is. This is the first document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The ribbon as the one we can see round the left arm of this soldier, does it -- is it like the ones you found in Lazete 1 by its size and shape and by the quality of the cloth?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: It is difficult to make those determinations, obviously because it's an image. But it appears to be similar to those that were found in the graves, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please get the next still.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, here, in this still, this member of the BH army is wearing on his head, or, actually, on his forehead a piece of cloth. Would such pieces of cloth be also like the ones you found in Lazete 1?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: I think only as far as it's a piece of cloth. It doesn't seem to be too similar to the ones we found. But it appears to be a piece of cloth around his forehead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be possible for such a cloth to be found to -- at that part of the head where the eyes were upon the decay of soft tissue?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: Because of decomposition and the movement of the bodies, yes, the pieces of cloth, in some cases, did move.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I know that this is a pathologist's job which is done in a morgue, but I'm asking you due to your expertise anyway, whether, with regard to the bodies in Lazete 1 and 2, you were able to observe injuries that may have been due to fire from larger-calibre weapons or mines and explosive devices?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: No, we would not be able to determine that. What we documented were fractures that existed previous to the recovery of the body or holes as they were simplified in the -- in the body recovery form. And that is documented, and -- and can be counted. As far as larger -- I guess what you mean by larger weapons is bigger than a small projectile from a rifle or explosives or mines of any type, I don't remember that we saw that evidence on the bodies, again, in the field, while the bodies were in situ.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, let us look at 1D01358 from the 65 ter list. Professor, you can look what you have in front of you, but this document is also in e-court. If I understand correctly, this is a publication of the British Forensic Sciences Academy from July 2006. Please look at paragraphs 2 and 3 on this page. The authors, stated above, put forward the results of their analysis. They said that they sent a questionnaire to 65 forensic pathologists who have been involved in the ICTY missions. The rate of answer was 38 per cent. Whereas, 18 did not know how the medical legal data were exploited by the ICTY; three of them have been subjected to pressures, as we read here; three of them were aware of mass grave-sites wittingly not investigated by the ICTY; 15 considered that the ICTY respected the elementary rules of law; and four of them questioned the impartiality of the justice led by the ICTY. Did you, at any point, get this questionnaire to fill in about your work?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to see this analysis and the report?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does the name of the author of this paper mean anything to you within the circles of your expertise; and did you have an occasion to familiarise yourself with his work?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I don't know what you're asking. I see -- I don't know what is on your question list and I don't know whether you prepared it yourself. But I see four authors. Were you referring to all four or... or have you not looked at it? Because you're asking about "the author."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. There are four authors listed in the heading, and that's what I see in front of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you asked about "the author," and familiarise yourself with his work, which doesn't refer to a plurality. Witness, are the names Lorin De la Grandmaison, Durigon, Moutel, or Herve, are they familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they are not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic. You said ten minutes or less. It's -- we're now at 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, I'm going to conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to thank the Professor for the answers he has given us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You have concluded, therefore, Mr. Stojanovic? Ms. MacGregor, could you give us an indication as to how much time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: It will be a very brief re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Brief is a flexible term as I've learned in my work here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Can you give me just one moment to confer with Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one question on re-direct which I can ask now before we go on any break, if you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the Defence. If we would allow the Prosecution to put that one question to the witness, if there's no follow-up we could adjourn for the day after that. I'm looking at you, Mr. Stojanovic; I'm looking at Mr. Mladic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Mr. Peccerelli, in your report on Lazete 1, you conclude that the strips of cloth found in and around the grave-site were of similar material, colour and length. And I wonder how did those pieces of cloth compare in terms of material, colour and length with the strips of cloth found in Lazete 2?

utterances.speaker: FREDY PECCERELLI
utterances.text: They were the same. They were pink scalloped materials. We found over 30 in the grave fill not associated to bodies in both graves and, as I mentioned, 89 immediately around the head. So they were very similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MACGREGOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. MacGregor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one very short question for you, Witness. In your report you used the expression "live rounds." What do you exactly understand by live round?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Live rounds were the combination of the bullet casing and the bullet still in place, so these were either duds or were not fired and fell to the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Have the questions in re-examination or the question by the Bench -- no need for further examination. Mr. Peccerelli, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. It's -- it's a pleasure to be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 29th of October, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III -- Courtroom I. We move to Courtroom I. In the other courtroom; that is, Courtroom I. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of October, 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
